text:
Tomas Hertl plays under 16 minutes a night, and in those minutes Vegas has been dominant. At five-on-five the Golden Knights get almost 64% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), about 13.8 points better than when he sits.

His scoring isn't a fluke either. He has 9 goals on 9.3 expected, 17 points in 22 games, and a seven-game point streak with 4 goals and 5 assists. His rate of 2.94 points per 60 minutes is at the top of our range for him, so a little cooling would be normal, but nothing here leans on luck.

Last season, Evolving-Hockey credited most of his value to the power play, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 32% of his entries, so his line works off dump-ins and the forecheck. His 59 hits fit that. One flashpoint: a hit on Nashville's Mavrik Bourque on Nov. 13 drew Ryan O'Reilly's anger and talk of a Player Safety look, per Markerzone; he played two nights later. Watch whether his minutes grow to match the results.
headline: Hertl's line is winning its minutes
